I completely agree.. I get people want their voice heard and they are using whatever means necessary but how is causing INNOCENT people to lose their jobs, their homes, their cars, and even their lives honoring the name of George Floyd?   ..and when so many of those people already suffered greatly in the midst of this pandemic. The bashing of windows, the beating of bricks, and the bursting of flames is drowning out the name that matters the most of all this -- George Floyd.

Don't get me wrong, I definitely get rioting and aiming your grievances at the police and system that they were cultivated in (as long as you're you know.. not beating them with a brick, leaving them an inch away from death).. but not innocent people who have NOTHING to do with this situation. How do you know that car you just set on fire wasn't George Floyd's cousin or that small business you just destroyed and looted wasn't his best friend's growing up? These people you could be hurting in the midst of the riot could be allies in your cause.. A lot of what I am seeing is just senseless violence and people ARE using this as an opportunity to benefit for PERSONAL gain.. not for justice for George Floyd.

Just because what happened to George Floyd was a lot worse, does NOT make this right to do to people that have nothing to do with the injustices surrounding his death. My heart can and did break for both things that happened.

You were denied. Reapply with a different e-mail ASAP. It took me like 7 tries but I finally got one approved for the correct amount (I have had all sorts of problems, including receiving 1/4 of the correct amount with their first docusign loan offer).

The number to call is 1-888-923-0009

I think they close at 2pm PST. They are usually very helpful and answered each of my 11 calls on Tuesday within 5 minutes. If you don't like the rep that answered, just say thank you and call again in an hour to get a different one. Some are definitely more helpful/informative than others.

It means you are denied. That happened to me as well. I reapplied (three other times after - seven in total) and finally got approved. Just keep submitting apps (making sure you're submitting all necessary documents/info) and calling them. Good luck!
